original_question: If a field F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.3 in §2 (“Other problems regarding crossed products”): “If F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every central simple F-algebra a crossed product?”
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It has the correct hypothesis on the field F (cohomological dimension at most 2), the correct class of objects (central simple F-algebras), and the correct property being asked about (whether they are crossed products). In fact, it matches Problem 2.3 almost verbatim.
missing_details: The paper presents this as an open problem, specifically Problem 2.3 in §2, not as a theorem or conjecture.
To be fully stand-alone, “central simple F-algebra” should be unpacked as a finite-dimensional F-algebra with center F and no nontrivial two-sided ideals (§0, p. 2).

To be fully stand-alone, “crossed product” should be defined as follows: if A has degree n, then A is a crossed product when it contains a maximal commutative étale F-subalgebra of degree n over F that is Galois over F (§0, p. 2).

The paper also makes explicit that this can be reformulated in terms of the associated division algebra: a central simple algebra is a crossed product if and only if its associated division algebra is (§0, p. 3).

If one wants the question to be completely self-contained for readers outside the paper, the term “cohomological dimension” should be specified, since the paper uses it here but does not re-define it locally.
refined_question: Let F be a field with cohomological dimension at most 2. Is every finite-dimensional central simple F-algebra A over F a crossed product; that is, does A contain a maximal commutative étale F-subalgebra L/F of degree deg(A) that is Galois over F?
equivalent_formulation: If F has cohomological dimension at most 2, is every F-division algebra a crossed product?
justification: The draft is targeting §2, Problem 2.3 (p. 5), and not a broader neighboring problem: the paper asks exactly whether fields of cohomological dimension at most 2 force all central simple algebras to be crossed products. The immediately preceding sentence in §2 explains the intent: all known examples of non-crossed-product algebras occur over fields of cohomological dimension at least 3, which is why the cd(F) ≤ 2 case is isolated as the natural next case. To make the question truly stand-alone, one must import the definitions from §0: “central simple F-algebra” from the Basic Definitions paragraph (p. 2), and “crossed product” from the Definition of a crossed product paragraph (p. 2). Section 0 also explicitly supplies the only paper-sanctioned alternate formulation: asking about all central simple algebras is equivalent to asking about their associated F-division algebras (§0, The crossed product problem for division algebras, p. 3).
